title: Pascha on Sunday vs fourteenth moon — indifferent rite; Victor vs Irenaeus; Quartodecimans mislabeled heretics
source_text: XXII. Nec majorem vim habet alia instantia, quam affert Bellarminus de Paschate. quod, inquit, credendum est in Novo Testamento celebrandum esse die Dominico non decima quarta Lunae, quocunque die inciderit, licet de eo in sacra Scriptura nihil extet. Fatemur enim quidem in Scriptura nihil de ista re haberi, sed dicimus quoque rem per se indifferentem esse, quae solum ad ritus externos Ecclesiae pertinet, non vero ad ea unde salus pendet. Olim quidem hac de re altero post Christum saeculo, excitata est magna controversia inter Ecclesiam Romanam & Asiaticas Ecclesias, ut propterea sese mutuo excommunicarent. Sed quamvis consuetudo Ecclesiae Romanae, quae tandem ubique obtinuit, rationi magis consentanea videatur, tamen hac in re utrinque peccatum est. Ideoque Irenaeus Episcopus Lugdunensis circa illa tempora graviter reprehendit Victorem Episcopum Romanum, quod tanto ardore de re non magni momenti certaret, & nimium de levi causa charitatis vinculum cum Orientalibus Ecclesiis abrumperet. In catalogis quidem haereticorum, quos patres texuerunt, recensentur Quartodecimani. Sed quicunque catalogos istos diligentius inspiciet, videbit patres illos inter haereses numerare opiniones quascunque ab ipsis improbatas, quamvis de rebus levibus & minime necessariis.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does another instance which Bellarmine brings about the Pasch have greater force — namely, that it must be believed that in the New Testament it is to be celebrated on the Lord's Day, not on the fourteenth of the Moon, whichever day it falls, although nothing on this exists in sacred Scripture. For we indeed confess that nothing on that matter is had in Scripture, but we also say that the matter is in itself indifferent, belonging only to the external rites of the Church, not to those things on which salvation depends. Formerly indeed on this matter in the second century after Christ a great controversy was stirred between the Roman Church and the Asian Churches, so that for that reason they mutually excommunicated one another. But although the custom of the Roman Church, which at last obtained everywhere, may seem more agreeable to reason, yet on this point there is sin on both sides. And therefore Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyons, about those times gravely rebuked Victor, Bishop of Rome, because he contended with such heat about a matter of no great moment, and too much for a light cause broke the bond of charity with the Eastern Churches. In the catalogs of heretics which the fathers composed, the Quartodecimans are indeed listed. But whoever inspects those catalogs more carefully will see that those fathers number among heresies whatever opinions they disapproved, even about light and least necessary matters.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's Pascha instance — Sunday, not the fourteenth moon, though Scripture is silent — has no more force.
We grant the silence; we deny the stake: the day is indifferent, a church rite, not a salvation hinge.
Second-century Rome and Asia even excommunicated each other over it.
Rome's custom may look wiser, yet both sides sinned in the heat.
Irenaeus rebuked Victor for rupturing charity over a light cause.
Fathers' catalogs list Quartodecimans as heretics, but they often brand as heresy any view they dislike — even on trivial points.
